raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #7401. When a checkpoint is saved exactly at an epoch boundary (e.g. `save_freq` is a multiple of `steps_per_epoch`), resuming silently skips the next epoch: the job can exit with status 0 having performed none of the remaining updates, leaving an under-trained model that looks "complete".

**Root cause:** the saved `StatefulDataLoader` state marks the sampler as fully exhausted. On resume, the trainer already advances to the next epoch (`start_epoch = global_step // steps_per_epoch`) and calls `set_epoch()` before iterating; the restored iterator then fast-forwards the *new* epoch's sampler by the whole epoch length (torchdata restores the sampler position via `itertools.islice`), so the new epoch yields 0 batches.

**Fix:** #5725 solved the same bug for `ppo/ray_trainer.py` with a modulo check (`global_steps % steps_per_epoch == 0`). This PR applies the same, already-accepted approach to the remaining affected paths:

- `verl/utils/checkpoint/checkpoint_handler.py` (shared by SFT spmd/ray trainers): new optional `steps_per_epoch` argument; skip restoring the dataloader state when `resume_global_step % steps_per_epoch == 0`. Detection is disabled when the argument is not provided, so existing behavior is unchanged for other callers.
- `verl/trainer/sft_trainer.py` / `verl/trainer/sft_trainer_ray.py`: pass `steps_per_epoch` through.
- `verl/trainer/ppo/v1/trainer_base.py`: same boundary check as `ppo/ray_trainer.py`, using the trainer's own `steps_per_epoch` (consistent with its `current_epoch` computation).

**Relation to #7402 (why this is not a duplicate):** #7402 addresses the same issue but introduces a new on-disk sidecar metadata file (~50 lines plus format versioning and a legacy path), which only protects *newly written* checkpoints and adds a new hard failure (`ValueError`) when resuming with a different `steps_per_epoch` (e.g. different GPU count after preemption). This PR is the minimal fix: no new artifact, works for every existing checkpoint, adds no new failure mode, and also covers `ppo/v1/trainer_base.py`, which #7402 does not touch. Related: #5725, #7402, #7516.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+dataloader+epoch+boundary
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)

### Test

Added `tests/utils/ckpt/test_checkpoint_handler_epoch_boundary_on_cpu.py` (9 cases, matches the `tests/**/test_*_on_cpu.py` pattern so it is picked up by `cpu_unit_tests.yml` automatically):

```bash
python -m pytest tests/utils/ckpt/test_checkpoint_handler_epoch_boundary_on_cpu.py -q
# 9 passed
```

Covers: boundary detection on/off/mid-epoch/first-epoch steps, and `_load_dataloader_state` end-to-end (stale state dropped at boundary / restored mid-epoch / restored when detection disabled / missing file starts from scratch).

Also validated end-to-end with a real `StatefulDataLoader` (torchdata 0.11.0, `num_workers=2`) reproducing the verl loop (`set_epoch` + `iter` per epoch, saving inside the loop body before `StopIteration`): without the fix the resumed epoch yields **0 batches**; with the fix it yields the full epoch.

Observed in production: a 4-epoch Megatron SFT job preempted at global step 4225 resumed from `global_step_3183` (`3 × steps_per_epoch`) and exited SUCCEEDED after 0 training steps; only 3 epoch checkpoints existed while 4 were configured.

### API and Usage Example

No API changes. `CheckpointHandler` gains an optional keyword argument `steps_per_epoch` (default `None` = detection off, fully backward compatible). No user action is required.

```python
# SFT trainers already wire this up internally; no user-side change.
# For direct CheckpointHandler users who want the protection:
handler = CheckpointHandler(
    engine=engine,
    train_dataloader=train_dataloader,
    default_local_dir=ckpt_dir,
    steps_per_epoch=len(train_dataloader),  # optional; enables epoch-boundary detection
)
```

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/utils/checkpoint/checkpoint_handler.py`: optional `steps_per_epoch`; `_at_epoch_boundary()` helper; `_load_dataloader_state()` logs a warning and skips the stale restore at epoch boundaries.
- `verl/trainer/sft_trainer.py`, `verl/trainer/sft_trainer_ray.py`: pass `steps_per_epoch` (both call sites are after `steps_per_epoch` is computed).
- `verl/trainer/ppo/v1/trainer_base.py`: same boundary check as `ppo/ray_trainer.py` (#5725), based on the trainer's own `steps_per_epoch`.
- `tests/utils/ckpt/test_checkpoint_handler_epoch_boundary_on_cpu.py`: new unit tests (9 cases).

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting): all hooks pass (ruff, ruff-format, mypy, autogen-trainer-cfg, license, docstrings, etc.).
- [x] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs): not applicable — bug fix restoring expected behavior, no user-facing API or config change.
- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to [the CI workflow](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows) to cover all the code: new CPU unit tests auto-discovered by `cpu_unit_tests.yml` (`tests/**/test_*_on_cpu.py`).
- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in [the `ci-request` channel](https://verl-project.slack.com/archives/C091TCESWB1) in [the `verl` Slack workspace](https://join.slack.com/t/verl-project/shared_invite/zt-3855yhg8g-CTkqXu~hKojPCmo7k_yXTQ).
- [x] Recipe submodule: not related.

Why this is not a duplicate: see "Relation to #7402" — materially different approach (minimal modulo check as already merged in #5725 vs. a new on-disk sidecar format), plus coverage of `ppo/v1/trainer_base.py`. Test commands and results: listed in the Test section (9/9 passed, plus the end-to-end before/after comparison).

nodes.body:
I think the V1 part of this change introduces a data-order regression, and V1 already handles the epoch boundary correctly without it.

**Why V1 doesn't need the skip:** `_fetch_one_gen_batch` catches `StopIteration` and calls `iter()` again. On a boundary resume, the first `iter()` applies the saved (exhausted) state and stops immediately. The second `iter()` starts a fresh epoch from the restored sampler. So no epoch is lost.

**Why skipping is harmful for the RL sampler:** `create_rl_sampler` uses torchdata's `RandomSampler` with a `torch.Generator`, and that generator's state is part of `data.pt`. If restore is skipped, the new dataloader starts from the generator's initial state, so the epoch after resume replays epoch 1's permutation exactly. An uninterrupted run would draw a new one. This happens with `data.seed: null` too, because an unseeded `torch.Generator()` starts from a fixed default seed. The SFT path uses `DistributedSampler` with `set_epoch`, which reseeds per epoch, so I believe skipping is fine there; this only concerns the RL samplers.

**GPU check:** main @ 3c6d9b4, V1 trainer, Qwen3-0.6B, 64 GSM8K prompts, batch 32 → 2 steps/epoch, `total_epochs=2`. The checkpoint is saved at step 2 (epoch boundary) and resumed with `resume_mode=auto`. The values below are the first 8 sorted dataset indices of each training batch:

| run | step 3 | step 4 |
|---|---|---|
| uninterrupted | `[4, 6, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14]` | `[0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 15]` |
| resume, main | `[4, 6, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14]` | `[0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 15]` |
| resume, this PR's V1 change | `[0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 13, 14]` (= step 1) | `[2, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 15]` (= step 2) |

On main, steps 3–4 run and match the uninterrupted run. With the skip, epoch 2 repeats epoch 1.

The legacy `ray_trainer.py` has the same replay since #5725. A fix that keeps the state is to restore it and then drain the exhausted epoch when `global_steps % steps_per_epoch == 0` (`for _ in dataloader: pass`), so the next `for batch in dataloader` starts a fresh permutation. I have that with a CPU test locally and can open it separately if useful. Given the legacy trainer is deprecated, it may not be worth it, though.

Suggestion: drop the `trainer_base.py` hunk from this PR (or limit the skip to samplers without generator state).

- `verl/trainer/ppo/v1/trainer_base.py`: same boundary check as `ppo/ray_trainer.py` (#5725), based on the trainer's own `steps_per_epoch`.

+"""Check V1 checkpoint data order using the real sampler, loader, and trainer methods."""
+
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+from omegaconf import OmegaConf
+from torchdata.stateful_dataloader import StatefulDataLoader
+
+from verl.trainer.ppo.utils import create_rl_sampler
+from verl.trainer.ppo.v1.trainer_base import PPOTrainer
+
+
+class _StubTrainer(PPOTrainer):
+    """Disable callbacks while exercising the production V1 dataloader path."""
+
+    def on_step_end(self):
+        """Skip step callbacks in the dataloader-only test trainer."""
+        pass
+
+    def on_sample_end(self):
+        """Skip sample callbacks in the dataloader-only test trainer."""
+        pass
+
+
+def _make_trainer(checkpoint_dir, seed, num_workers):
+    """Build a minimal V1 trainer with a real random sampler and stateful loader."""
+    # Bypass model/worker initialization, but exercise the production checkpoint
+    # loader and _fetch_one_gen_batch, including its StopIteration handling.
+    trainer = _StubTrainer.__new__(_StubTrainer)
+    dataset = [{"index": index, "raw_prompt": index} for index in range(64)]
+    sampler = create_rl_sampler(OmegaConf.create({"shuffle": True, "seed": seed}), dataset)
+    trainer.train_dataloader = StatefulDataLoader(
+        dataset, batch_size=8, sampler=sampler, num_workers=num_workers, drop_last=True
+    )
+    trainer.train_dataloader_it = None
+    trainer.steps_per_epoch = len(trainer.train_dataloader)
+    trainer.global_steps = 0
+    trainer.trainer_mode = "sync"
+    trainer.use_critic = False
+    trainer.actor_rollout_wg = MagicMock()
+    trainer.config = OmegaConf.create(
+        {
+            "trainer": {
+                "resume_mode": "resume_path",
+                "resume_from_path": str(checkpoint_dir),
+                "del_local_ckpt_after_load": False,
+            }
+        }
+    )
+    return trainer
+
+
+def _fetch_indices(trainer, count):
+    """Fetch batches and return their dataset indices in traversal order."""
+    return [trainer._fetch_one_gen_batch()["index"].tolist() for _ in range(count)]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "seed,checkpoint_step,num_workers",
+    [(42, 3, 0), (None, 3, 0), (42, 8, 0), (None, 8, 0)],
+)
+def test_resume_preserves_batch_order(tmp_path, seed, checkpoint_step, num_workers):
+    """Preserve V1 sample order across mid-epoch and epoch-boundary resumes."""
+    checkpoint_dir = tmp_path / f"global_step_{checkpoint_step}"
+    checkpoint_dir.mkdir()
+    continuous = _make_trainer(checkpoint_dir, seed, num_workers)
+    steps_per_epoch = continuous.steps_per_epoch
+    total_steps = 3 * steps_per_epoch
+
+    expected = _fetch_indices(continuous, checkpoint_step)
+    # Save inside the last batch body, before asking the iterator for
+    # StopIteration, just like a checkpoint at the end of a training step.
+    torch.save(continuous.train_dataloader.state_dict(), checkpoint_dir / "data.pt")
+    expected += _fetch_indices(continuous, total_steps - checkpoint_step)
+    assert expected[:steps_per_epoch] != expected[steps_per_epoch : 2 * steps_per_epoch]
+
+    resumed = _make_trainer(checkpoint_dir, seed, num_workers)
+    resumed._load_checkpoint()
+    assert resumed.global_steps == checkpoint_step
+    actual = expected[:checkpoint_step] + _fetch_indices(resumed, total_steps - checkpoint_step)
+
+    # Dropping the exhausted state loses RandomSampler's RNG progress and
+    # replays epoch 0, including when seed=None creates a fresh Generator.
+    assert actual == expected

+    def _make_handler(self, monkeypatch, steps_per_epoch, resume_global_step, train_dataloader=None, dp_rank=0):

issue_comments.body:
I think the V1 part of this change introduces a data-order regression, and V1 already handles the epoch boundary correctly without it.

**Why V1 doesn't need the skip:** `_fetch_one_gen_batch` catches `StopIteration` and calls `iter()` again. On a boundary resume, the first `iter()` applies the saved (exhausted) state and stops immediately. The second `iter()` starts a fresh epoch from the restored sampler. So no epoch is lost.

**Why skipping is harmful for the RL sampler:** `create_rl_sampler` uses torchdata's `RandomSampler` with a `torch.Generator`, and that generator's state is part of `data.pt`. If restore is skipped, the new dataloader starts from the generator's initial state, so the epoch after resume replays epoch 1's permutation exactly. An uninterrupted run would draw a new one. This happens with `data.seed: null` too, because an unseeded `torch.Generator()` starts from a fixed default seed. The SFT path uses `DistributedSampler` with `set_epoch`, which reseeds per epoch, so I believe skipping is fine there; this only concerns the RL samplers.

**GPU check:** main @ 3c6d9b4, V1 trainer, Qwen3-0.6B, 64 GSM8K prompts, batch 32 → 2 steps/epoch, `total_epochs=2`. The checkpoint is saved at step 2 (epoch boundary) and resumed with `resume_mode=auto`. The values below are the first 8 sorted dataset indices of each training batch:

| run | step 3 | step 4 |
|---|---|---|
| uninterrupted | `[4, 6, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14]` | `[0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 15]` |
| resume, main | `[4, 6, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14]` | `[0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 15]` |
| resume, this PR's V1 change | `[0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 13, 14]` (= step 1) | `[2, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 15]` (= step 2) |

On main, steps 3–4 run and match the uninterrupted run. With the skip, epoch 2 repeats epoch 1.

The legacy `ray_trainer.py` has the same replay since #5725. A fix that keeps the state is to restore it and then drain the exhausted epoch when `global_steps % steps_per_epoch == 0` (`for _ in dataloader: pass`), so the next `for batch in dataloader` starts a fresh permutation. I have that with a CPU test locally and can open it separately if useful. Given the legacy trainer is deprecated, it may not be worth it, though.

Suggestion: drop the `trainer_base.py` hunk from this PR (or limit the skip to samplers without generator state).

📝 Summary
## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Resuming training from a mid-epoch checkpoint now preserves the dataloader’s batch order, so training continues from the expected point. * Resuming from an epoch-boundary checkpoint now starts with a fresh dataloader rather than reusing stale saved state. * Checkpoint resume behavior is consistent across CPU training configurations and supported data-parallel settings, including runs with different replica counts and ranks. The checkpoint handler now receives `steps_per_epoch` from both SFT trainers. At a positive epoch boundary, it skips restoring saved dataloader state. New CPU tests cover boundary detection, state restoration, and resumed batch-order continuity. **Changes: Epoch-Boundary Resume** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |:---|:---| |**Boundary-aware dataloader restoration**

**Security Blast Radius** - _inferred_ — The changed decision affects dataloader continuation for the selected training checkpoint.
